This was the 'wisdom of the hands,' an ancient, unspoken language passed down through generations of potters. But in a city increasingly governed by the rigid calipers and unforgiving plumb lines of the 'Standard,' Sela's art was becoming a heresy. Her work was beautiful, functional, desired by many, but it was not uniform. And in the eyes of the Keepers of the Standard, that was a crime.
